title: The Chamber Where Asking Becomes Dangerous

features.name: archive's own ledger
features.desc-on-touch: You find questions the archive asked itself about what should be preserved and what should be forgotten. The asking never yielded answers, only more dangerous questions.

features.name: threshold-pulse chamber
features.desc-on-touch: You feel something in the archive asking harder now, pushing against its own boundaries, its rhythm a pressure that will not settle.

features.name: forbidden archive door
features.desc-on-touch: You stand before it: in every archive that chooses what to keep, there is a door. Behind it, the questions that would unmake the whole thing if asked aloud.

features.name: maker's argument residue
features.desc-on-touch: You hear them still: Leif arguing for breadth, Katita arguing for depth. The archive holds their voices, still asking: were we right? The question vibrates here, dangerous and alive.

features.name: corruption-boundary marker
features.desc-on-touch: You sense where the archive's safe questions end and the dangerous ones begin. The boundary is not a wall; it is a frequency, a tone, a pressure you can feel in the static.

features.name: silence-keeper stone
features.desc-on-touch: You touch what the archive chose not to ask itself. The weight of that silence is held here like a stone, heavy and warm, dangerous because it will not speak.

inscription: here asking learned to carry the weight of what it might uncover

reverie.title: REVERIE — the tent where dangerous questions arrived
narr: You both sit in darkness. He asks: what if the archive
becomes able to ask questions we cannot answer? She asks:
what if we cannot stop it? The static crackles. He says:
then we will have made something that thinks. She reaches
past the dark. I am afraid of that, she says. So am I,
he says. They sit. The questions wait in the silence.
